title: A Committee of Creditors Cannot Withdraw an Approved Resolution Plan Once It Is Before the NCLT: Supreme Court
case_name: Bank of India & Ors. v. S.M. Kamal Pasha & Ors.
card_summary: Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held that once a committee of creditors approves a resolution plan and places it before the NCLT, the committee cannot withdraw that approval merely because the corporate debtor's cash position has since improved. The NCLAT had reversed an NCLT order allowing withdrawal, and the Supreme Court agreed the Code gives no one power to withdraw an approved plan at this stage.
card_tip: Once a plan clears CoC approval, treat it as locked in; an improved balance sheet is no ground to reopen it, and any windfall argument must go to the adjudicating authority, not a late withdrawal bid.
verification_notes: LiveLaw, LawChakra and LawBeat all report the same bench, the 26 October 2026 date, the NCLT's reversal by NCLAT, and the holding that an approved plan cannot be withdrawn at the CoC's instance once before the adjudicating authority. The approved plan value (Rs 172.55 crore) and the appellants' windfall argument are reported consistently; the Court's direction to the NCLT to decide the plan-approval and OTS applications together is noted in LiveLaw and LawChakra. Full judgment text not independently reviewed.
